title: "Resources"
order: 122
---

This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched
for it. It's pure assembly — one real CMDB entry and service-catalog entry for the eQMS
(electronic quality-management system), built from every crosswalk this course's first three
modules already locked, then tested against three reviewers this curriculum already built in
depth elsewhere. The links below are the direct inputs this module draws on; read any of them for
the actual mechanics, citations, and reasoning this lesson references by name but doesn't
redevelop.

- **[ITIL-to-QSE crosswalk: CMDB and continual
  improvement](../itil-to-qse-crosswalk-cmdb-and-continual-improvement/index.qmd)** — this
  course's own module 2, where the eQMS's CMDB entry (with its blank qualification field) and
  service-catalog entry (with the Fairview document-control inconsistency) were first built.
  Read it for the exact field-by-field artifacts this module reconciles.

- **[ITIL-to-GRC crosswalk](../itil-to-grc-crosswalk/index.qmd)** — this course's own module 3,
  which first recognized that the CMDB's blank qualification field already has its answer in the
  eQMS's RMF (Risk Management Framework) file, and honestly mapped the eQMS's three RMF control
  families against ISO/IEC 27001's Annex A domains, finding one clean match and two domains with
  no counterpart at all. Read it for the full domain-by-domain reasoning this module's security-
  assessor test relies on.

- **[Categorize and select
  controls](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/categorize-and-select-controls/index.qmd)**
  and **[authorize and
  monitor](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/authorize-and-monitor/index.qmd)** (both
  `grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`) — the eQMS's full RMF file: its moderate-impact
  categorization, its three control families, and its standing monitoring plan. This is the
  actual content now cross-referenced from the CMDB's qualification field; read either module for
  the verbatim NIST text and the full reasoning behind the moderate-impact finding.

- **[The AABB assessment
  process](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/the-aabb-assessment-process/index.qmd)** — how an AABB
  (Association for the Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies) assessor actually runs a QSE-based
  review, including how a self-identified, actively-managed gap grades differently than one the
  assessor finds cold. This module's AABB-assessor test applies that lens directly.

- **[FDA inspection authority and
  outcomes](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/fda-inspection-authority-and-outcomes/index.qmd)** and
  **[warning letters and
  recalls](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/warning-letters-and-recalls/index.qmd)** — what an FDA
  investigator actually checks during a routine or for-cause inspection, and how an unreconciled
  documentation inconsistency becomes a Form 483 observation. This module's FDA-investigator test
  applies both directly, without redeveloping either.

- **[Reading a SOC 2
  report](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/reading-a-soc-2-report/index.qmd)** and
  **[reading an ISO 27001
  certificate](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)**
  (both `vendor-and-third-party-risk-management`) — what a security assessor actually looks for
  in a SOC 2 or ISO 27001-style review. This module's honest conclusion — that the reconciled
  artifact is strong partial evidence for this reviewer, not a complete answer — leans directly on
  the domain gaps these two modules and `itil-to-grc-crosswalk` already found.
